title: Grateful Dead Live at Palace Theater on 1972-09-23
lineage: SBD> MR> Cass> DAT> CDR> EAC> SHN

ai_review.summary: Warm soundboard captures a high‑energy September 1972 show with a smoking The Other One, roaring China>Rider and the legendary Cryptical/Other One sequence.
ai_review.review: This recording is a solid SBD that delivers most of its warmth and clarity after an uneven opening mix.  The band is on fire – Jerry’s flanged leads, Phil’s bass bombs and Keith’s early‑’70s chops drive a second set packed with a monster Other One, Cryptical Envelopment and tight classics like Big River and Sugar Magnolia.

ai_rating.rationale: Over 25 reviews overwhelmingly positive (average ≈4.3 stars).  Consistently high praise for the performance and generally good soundboard quality, with only minor technical complaints.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Warm SBD with some tape hiss and a slightly muddy first‑set mix (Phil forward, drums buried).  Mix settles by the second set; overall clarity and instrument separation are solid for a 1972 board.

standout_songs: Cryptical Envelopment > Drums > The Other One > Wharf Rat
China Cat Sunflower > I Know You Rider
poor_songs: First set (overall – noted as lagging by some reviewers)
show_quality.setlist_flow: A strong first half that builds into a blistering second set; transitions such as China>Rider and the long Other One sequence are highlighted.  The show runs long (~200 min) but maintains momentum.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Described as “on fire”, using flanger/wa‑wa, delivering powerful leads throughout especially on The Other One and Sugar Magnolia.
band_member_comments.Phil: Bass is front‑forward, noted for “bass bombs” and a Brubeck‑style tribute during The Other One; occasional front‑mix dominance early in the show.
band_member_comments.Bob: Vocal mix praised (especially Bobby’s scream at end of The Other One); overall solid rhythm guitar work.
band_member_comments.Keys: Early Keith is highlighted as sounding “great”, tearing it up, with some reviewers noting his early‑’70s keyboard texture; Donna’s vocals noted as nice later in the set.
band_member_comments.Drums: Bill (drums) gets a shout‑out for an excellent solo after Cryptical Envelopment and solid overall drive.
